title: 550. The Road to 1066: Rise of the Normans (Part 3)

sentences.en: At the end of France, there is a plain filled with woods and fruit trees.
sentences.zh: 在法国的尽头，有一片长满树木和果树的平原。

sentences.en: In this narrow place, there lived a great number of very tough, strong people, the name of whom was Normans.
sentences.zh: 在这个狭小的地方，曾生活着大量非常强悍、坚韧的人，他们被称为诺曼人。

sentences.en: Such were their numbers that in time, as the population grew, the fields and orchards of Normandy proved insufficient to keep them all fed.
sentences.zh: 他们的人数如此之多，以至于随着时间推移人口增长，诺曼底的田野和果园已经不够养活他们所有人了。

sentences.en: Therefore, the Normans scattered here and there throughout all the various parts of the world, making their way into numerous regions and countries,
sentences.zh: 因此，诺曼人四处分散到世界各地，涌入许许多多的地区和国家，

sentences.en: abandoning what little they had in order to obtain very much more.
sentences.zh: 为了获得更多，他们抛弃了本就不多的所有。

sentences.en: These people departed their homes, but they did not follow the custom of most people who go through the world, entering into the service of others.
sentences.zh: 这些人离开了家园，但他们并不像世上大多数人那样四处奔波、依附他人为仆。

sentences.en: Rather, like warriors of old, their aim was to make everybody subject to them and under their lordship.
sentences.zh: 相反，正如古代的勇士一样，他们的目标是让所有人臣服于他们，受其统治。

sentences.en: And so they took up arms and broke the bond of peace.
sentences.zh: 于是他们拿起武器，打破了和平的契约。

sentences.en: And whether as a mass of infantrymen or on horseback, they proved themselves great in deeds.
sentences.zh: 无论是作为庞大的步兵还是骑马作战，他们都展现出了伟大的功绩。

sentences.en: So that was the terrifying opening to the history of the Normans, written, Tom, in the mid-11th century by a monk called Amartus.
sentences.zh: 这就是诺曼人历史那令人畏惧的开端，汤姆，它是由一位名叫阿马图斯的修道士在11世纪中期撰写的。

sentences.en: And as you have pointed out in your notes, this is very reminiscent of the way that, you know,
sentences.zh: 正如你在笔记中指出的那样，这非常让人联想到，你知道的，

sentences.en: when the Greeks wrote about the intrusion on the world scene of the Romans or the Chinese about the coming of the Mongols,
sentences.zh: 当希腊人写到罗马人闯入世界舞台，或是中国人写到蒙古人入侵时，

sentences.en: they would say, oh, my God, there's this extraordinary new people who are absolutely formidable, very frightening, very brutal.
sentences.zh: 他们会说，天哪，出现了一群极其了不起的新人类，他们完全是强大无比、极其可怕、极其残忍。

sentences.en: They kill everybody.
sentences.zh: 他们杀光所有人。

sentences.en: They, you know.
sentences.zh: 他们，你知道的。

sentences.en: Where they come from.
sentences.zh: 他们从哪里来。

sentences.en: Yeah, where they come from.
sentences.zh: 对，他们从哪里来。

sentences.en: And the Normans are greeted by writers beyond Normandy's borders with the same kind of awe and terror, aren't they?
sentences.zh: 诺曼底边界之外的作家们对诺曼人的到来也怀有同样敬畏和恐惧，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, kind of dread for reasons that Amartus spells out, because he says that the Normans are physically hardy, very tough, very strong.
sentences.zh: 是的，带着某种恐惧，原因正如阿马图斯详细说明的那样，因为他说诺曼人身体强健、非常坚韧、非常强壮。

sentences.en: So Amartus writes in Latin, but the version we have is translated into French.
sentences.zh: 阿马图斯是用拉丁语写的，但我们现在看到版本已被翻译成了法语。

sentences.en: And he specifies that the Normans have a lust for seigneurie, so lordship.
sentences.zh: 他明确指出，诺曼人对封建领地充满渴望，也就是统治权。

sentences.en: And that they have a particular aptitude for chivalry, so fighting on horseback, what will in due course come to be the attribute of a knight, chivalry.
sentences.zh: 他们对骑士精神有着特殊的才能，即骑马作战，这在日后将成为骑士的标志，也就是骑士精神。

sentences.en: But basically, they're going around on horses, kind of nicking other people's land and property.
sentences.zh: 但基本上，他们就是骑着马到处跑，顺走别人的土地和财产。

sentences.en: And also, of course, he's very impressed by their wanderlust, this sense that they're spilling out across the world,
sentences.zh: 当然，他对他们漫游的热情也印象深刻，这种向世界各地扩张的态势，

sentences.en: and that their goal is a kind of greatness, that they're not prepared to serve other people.
sentences.zh: 并且他们的目标是一种伟大，他们不甘为人臣服。

sentences.en: And Amartus is speaking from experience.
sentences.zh: 阿马图斯是凭经验而言的。

sentences.en: So he is a monk in Monte Cassino, the great abbey in central Italy, which we last heard of in the podcast, because Wojtek.
sentences.zh: 他是意大利中部伟大修道院卡西诺山的修道士，我们在之前的播客里最后一次听到它是因为沃伊泰克。

sentences.en: The bear, the Polish bear.
sentences.zh: 那只熊，那只波兰熊。

sentences.en: Yes, the Polish bear.
sentences.zh: 是的，那只波兰熊。

sentences.en: We're serving with the Polish army there in the Second World War.
sentences.zh: 我们在第二次世界大战中和波兰军队一起在那里服役。

sentences.en: But it's a very venerable abbey reaching back to the beginnings of Christianity in Italy.
sentences.zh: 但这是一座历史悠久的修道院，可以追溯到意大利基督教的萌芽时期。

sentences.en: And the fact that he is observing this from Italy is a reminder to us in England, we tend to think of the Norman conquest as the Normans are going one way.
sentences.zh: 他在意大利观察到这一点，对我们身在英国的人是一个提醒，我们往往认为诺曼征服是诺曼人单向的移动。

sentences.en: He has seen a great stream of Norman freebooters, adventurers, rogues, you know, mercenaries, whatever, heading south into Italy and beyond.
sentences.zh: 他看到了源源不断的诺曼自由民、冒险家、恶棍、你知道的，雇佣兵，诸如此类的人，正朝着意大利及更远的地方进发。

sentences.en: And actually, for me, one of the great fascinating stories of Normans is how they expand southwards and become a Mediterranean power.
sentences.zh: 事实上，对我们来说，诺曼人故事中最迷人的地方之一，就是他们如何向南扩张并成为地中海强权。

sentences.en: Well, because southern Italy in particular, I mean, if you're going out and you're looking for opportunities to set up your lordship,
sentences.zh: 嗯，尤其是因为南意大利，我的意思是，如果你出海寻找建立自己统治的机会，

sentences.en: then you want a place where there are going to be rich pickings.
sentences.zh: 那你就会想去一个有丰厚战利品的地方。

sentences.en: And southern Italy is perfect for the Normans' purpose, because this is a place where all kinds of different empires are rubbing up against each other.
sentences.zh: 而南意大利非常符合诺曼人的目的，因为这里是各种不同帝国相互碰撞的地方。

sentences.en: So there's Latin Christendom, but there is also the Byzantine Empire, so the Byzantines have territory there.
sentences.zh: 这里有拉丁基督教世界，但也有拜占庭帝国，拜占庭人在那里拥有领土。

sentences.en: And there's Muslim powers in Sicily and kind of constant ambitions to push up northwards through Italy.
sentences.zh: 西西里还有穆斯林势力，并且不断有着向北推进穿过意大利的野心。

sentences.en: So this is perfect for a bunch of kind of hardy horse riding mercenaries looking essentially to be paid and then to use that money to turn on the people who are paying them.
sentences.zh: 所以，这对于一帮强悍的骑马雇佣兵来说简直完美，他们本质上是为了拿报酬，然后用这些钱去对付那些付钱给他们的人。

sentences.en: And the first Normans who get hired in southern Italy are actually pilgrims returning from Jerusalem.
sentences.zh: 第一批在南意大利被雇佣的诺曼人其实是从耶路撒冷返回的朝圣者。

sentences.en: And they land on the heel of Italy in 1018 from Jerusalem and they get employed by rebels against Byzantine rule.
sentences.zh: 他们于1018年从耶路撒冷在意大利的“鞋跟”登陆，并被反抗拜占庭统治的叛军所雇佣。

sentences.en: So Italian speaking rebels.
sentences.zh: 也就是讲意大利语的叛军。

sentences.en: And then four years later, they've switched sides and they're in the service of the Byzantine Empire.
sentences.zh: 仅仅四年后，他们就倒戈了，开始为拜占庭帝国效力。

sentences.en: And then within a decade, these kind of Norman mercenaries, strongmen are carving out their own fiefdoMs.
sentences.zh: 在十年之内，这些诺曼雇佣兵和强人就开辟出了他们自己的封地。

sentences.en: And Amartus, from his vantage point in Monte Cassino, about halfway up Italy, you know, he's full of admiration, actually, for their kind of prowess, for their energy,
sentences.zh: 而阿马图斯站在位于意大利中部的卡西诺山这一有利位置上，你知道的，他对他们的英勇、他们的活力，

sentences.en: for their chutzpah, really, in just taking their opportunities.
sentences.zh: 以及他们抓住机遇的魄力，其实充满了敬佩。

sentences.en: But there are other monks at Monte Cassino who are slightly more jaundiced.
sentences.zh: 但卡西诺山的其他修道士则显得有些挑剔。

sentences.en: So the abbot of Monte Cassino is a guy called Desiderius, and he will actually go on to become pope.
sentences.zh: 卡西诺山的住持是一个叫德西德里乌斯的人，他后来真的当上了教皇。

sentences.en: And he views these Norman adventurers kind of as a wolf pack, that they've been driven southwards by hunger and they are hungry for blood.
sentences.zh: 他将这些诺曼冒险家视作一群狼，他们被饥饿驱赶向南方，渴望着鲜血。

sentences.en: So he wrote, the Normans are avid for rapine and possess an insatiable appetite for seizing what belongs to others.
sentences.zh: 因此他写道：诺曼人贪婪成性，对掠夺他人财物有着无法餍足的胃口。

sentences.en: It's not entirely wrong.
sentences.zh: 这并非完全错误。

sentences.en: Not entirely wrong.
sentences.zh: 并非完全错误。

sentences.en: And a perspective that others, as well as the Italians, will come to get.
sentences.zh: 这也是意大利人以及其他人后来都会获得的看法。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And I suppose a question that the Italians might have pondered was why didn't impecunious Normans, you know, if they're looking for lordships, why aren't they doing it nearer home?
sentences.zh: 我想意大利人可能会思考的一个问题是，为什么身无分文的诺曼人在寻找领地时，为什么不在离家近一点的地方这样做？

sentences.en: Why are they coming to Italy to do it?
sentences.zh: 为什么他们要来意大利这样做？

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: Well, let me just pause you there.
sentences.zh: 那么，我在这里暂停你一下。

sentences.en: So last time we heard about how Normandy was established.
sentences.zh: 上一次我们听说了诺曼底是如何建立的。

sentences.en: So that's under a guy called Rollo or Rolf.
sentences.zh: 那是建立在一个叫罗洛或罗尔夫的人统治之下。

sentences.en: Rolf.
sentences.zh: 罗尔夫。

sentences.en: Who, so we're talking about Northmen, Vikings, effectively, who have carved out and semi-being granted this territory in northern France by Charles the Simple.
sentences.zh: 所以我们讨论的是诺斯人，实际上就是维京人，他们在法兰西北部开辟了这片领地，并由“简单王”查理半授予了这片土地。

sentences.en: And that was in the early 10th century.
sentences.zh: 那是在10世纪初。

sentences.en: So Rollo died probably about 930.
sentences.zh: 所以罗洛大概在930年左右去世。

sentences.en: But now we've moved on a bit in time.
sentences.zh: 但现在我们的时间线稍微推移了一些。

sentences.en: So the last person that we met who was the kind of, the leader of the Normans was a guy called Richard II, Richard the Good.
sentences.zh: 我们最后见到的诺曼人领袖是一个叫理查二世的人，即“好人”理查。

sentences.en: So he's the brother-in-law of two other characters that we met last time, Ethel Reddy and Cnut.
sentences.zh: 他是我们在上一次节目中见到的另外两个人物——埃塞尔雷德和克努特的连襟。

sentences.en: And he had kept Normandy pretty settled, stable, secure.
sentences.zh: 他使诺曼底保持了相当的安定、稳定和安全。

sentences.en: And he's, of course, the brother as well of Emma of Normandy, who's got herself mixed up in all kinds of exciting dynastic shenanigans over in England,
sentences.zh: 当然，他也是诺曼底的埃玛的兄弟，埃玛自己卷入了英格兰各种激动人心的王朝阴谋之中，

sentences.en: which it would take another hour to explain.
sentences.zh: 如果要解释清楚这些，还得再花一个小时。

sentences.en: So Richard II in Normandy, things actually have been very ordered and secure under him, right?
sentences.zh: 所以在理查二世统治下的诺曼底，一切其实都非常井然有序且安全，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So, and the measure of this is that initially he'd begun life as the Count of Rouen, but he's kind of promoted himself to become the Duke of Normandy.
sentences.zh: 衡量这一点的是，他最初以鲁昂伯爵的身份开始人生，但后来他将自己晋升为诺曼底公爵。

sentences.en: And essentially by the end of his life, everyone else, including the King of France, has basically said, yeah, okay, you know, you can rank as a Duke.
sentences.zh: 基本上到他生命的尽头，其他所有人，包括法国国王，基本上都承认了：好吧，你可以享有公爵的头衔。

sentences.en: Or in Latin, a dux.
sentences.zh: 或者用拉丁语来说，叫 dux。

sentences.en: So this is the root of Duce, that, you know, the title that Mussolini takes up.
sentences.zh: 这就是“领袖（Duce）”一词的词根，你知道的，墨索里尼采用的那个头衔。

sentences.en: It's to be essentially a kind of military strongman as much as anything else.
sentences.zh: 本质上就是要做某种军事强人。

sentences.en: And in the context of France, there are five Dukes, as well as the Duke of Normandy.
sentences.zh: 在法国的语境下，除了诺曼底公爵外，还有另外四位公爵。

sentences.en: So the Duke of Burgundy, the Duke of Aquitaine, of Gascony, and directly on Normandy's Western Frank, the Duke of Brittany.
sentences.zh: 即勃艮第公爵、阿基坦公爵、加斯科涅公爵，以及紧邻诺曼底西线边境的布列塔尼公爵。

sentences.en: And to be a Duke in 11th century France is not the equivalent of being, say, an Earl in England, because we talked in the first episode about how,
sentences.zh: 在11世纪的法国担任公爵，不等同于在英格兰担任伯爵，因为我们在第一集里谈到过，

sentences.en: over the course of the 10th and into the 11th century,
sentences.zh: 在10世纪到11世纪的过程中，

sentences.en: the kings of England have massively consolidated and centralised their power over this kind of very precociously united kingdom.
sentences.zh: 英格兰国王在这个极早实现统一的王国里，大规模地巩固和集聚了他们的权力。

sentences.en: But in France, the opposite process has been happening.
sentences.zh: 但在法国，相反的过程正在发生。

sentences.en: Royal power has kind of ebbed and bled away.
sentences.zh: 王权在不断衰落和流失。

sentences.en: And by this point, so early 11th century in France, the king exercises direct rule only over a tiny patchwork of territories centred on Paris and Orléans.
sentences.zh: 到这个时候——也就是11世纪初的法国，国王直接统治的范围仅限于以巴黎和奥尔良为中心的细碎领地。

sentences.en: So to rule as the Duke of Normandy is to enjoy an autonomy, a kind of degree of independence that is beyond the wildest dreams of, you know,
sentences.zh: 因此，作为诺曼底公爵来统治，意味着享有自治权，一种远远超出东盎格利亚伯爵或麦西亚伯爵

sentences.en: the Earl of East Anglia or the Earl of Mercia.
sentences.zh: 最大胆梦想的独立程度。

sentences.en: And to give people a sense, I mean, it's far more than, let's say, I don't know, being the governor of a US state or something, because you're also an international player,
sentences.zh: 为了让大家有个概念，我的意思是，这远不止，比方说，担任某个美国州的州长之类的，因为你同时也是一个国际玩家，

sentences.en: aren't you?
sentences.zh: 对吧？

sentences.en: You can almost run your own foreign policy.
sentences.zh: 你几乎可以奉行你自己的外交政策。

sentences.en: Is that fair?
sentences.zh: 这么说公平吗？

sentences.en: Well, so we talked at the end of the last episode about how Richard's son, Robert, who rules as Duke for almost a decade, in 1035, he goes off on pilgrimage to Jerusalem.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们在上一集结尾时谈到，理查的儿子罗伯特，作为公爵统治了将近十年，在1035年，他启程前往耶路撒冷朝圣。

sentences.en: And we were expressing surprise at this because Normandy potentially would be in an unstable situation were he to die.
sentences.zh: 我们对此感到惊讶，因为如果他死了，诺曼底可能会陷入不稳定状态。

sentences.en: But one of the reasons he's going is undoubtedly because he's very pious.
sentences.zh: 但他成行的原因之一毫无疑问是因为他非常虔诚。

sentences.en: He wants to go to Jerusalem for those reasons.
sentences.zh: 出于这些原因，他想去耶路撒冷。

sentences.en: But also he wants to cut a dash.
sentences.zh: 但同时他也想出类拔萃一番。

sentences.en: He wants to display his wealth, his power, his authority on the grandest of international stages, which, if you're Christian, is Constantinople,
sentences.zh: 他想在最盛大的国际舞台上展示他的财富、权力和权威，而如果你是基督徒，那就是君士坦丁堡，

sentences.en: still the greatest city in the Christian world.
sentences.zh: 它依然是基督教世界中最伟大的城市。

sentences.en: And so he travels from Normandy to Constantinople and he cuts an absolutely amazing dash.
sentences.zh: 于是他从诺曼底旅行到君士坦丁堡，表现得极其惊艳。

sentences.en: You know, the Byzantines are really dazzled.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，拜占庭人真的被迷住了。

sentences.en: And this is despite the fact that they've had some dealings with the Normans in the south of Italy.
sentences.zh: 尽管他们之前在南意大利和诺曼人有过一些交道。

sentences.en: So they trust them, but they are impressed.
sentences.zh: 所以他们虽然有所防范，但仍然印象深刻。

sentences.en: And, you know, there are these reports that even his mules are shod with gold.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，有报道说甚至连他的骡子都钉着金马蹄。

sentences.en: And it's said that his campfires are fueled with the shells of pistachio nuts.
sentences.zh: 据说他的营地生火是用开心果壳作为燃料的。

sentences.en: And this is regarded even by the Byzantines as the height of the height of high living.
sentences.zh: 这甚至被拜占庭人视为奢华生活的最高境界。

sentences.en: And so they call him the Magnificent.
sentences.zh: 因此他们称他为“宏伟的罗伯特”。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: Which from a Byzantine paying, you know, paying tribute to a barbarian from the wild and frozen north is not bad.
sentences.zh: 这对于一个向来自冰冷荒蛮北方的野蛮人致敬的拜占庭政权来说，已经相当不错了。

sentences.en: I mean, that is kind of measure of his standing.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这某种程度上衡量了他的地位。

sentences.en: And yet Normandy itself is, you know, not remotely as rich and powerful as the Eastern Roman Empire, the Byzantine Empire, because not least because Normandy is embattled.
sentences.zh: 然而诺曼底本身，你知道的，远没有东罗马帝国、拜占庭帝国那么富裕和强大，很大程度上是因为诺曼底四面楚歌。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: It's surrounded by predators and rivals.
sentences.zh: 它被掠夺者和竞争对手包围着。

sentences.en: Yes, because the King of France doesn't exercise a kind of controlling authority.
sentences.zh: 是的，因为法国国王并不行使某种控制性的权威。

sentences.en: It means that all these various dukes and counts, if they're to rule their territory and perhaps expand them, they have to be very militarily proficient.
sentences.zh: 这意味着所有这些大大小小的公爵和伯爵，如果他们想统治自己的领土并加以扩张，就必须具备极高的军事造诣。

sentences.en: And they can't afford a single slip because, as you say, there are predators lurking everywhere.
sentences.zh: 他们容不得半点闪失，因为正如你所说，四处都潜伏着掠夺者。

sentences.en: So in the case of the Norman Dukes, these predators would include most obviously, I suppose, the King of France himself, because Paris is upriver from Rouen.
sentences.zh: 所以在诺曼公爵的案例中，这些掠夺者最明显的应该就是法国国王本人，因为巴黎位于鲁昂的上游。

sentences.en: And that's the great center of French royal power.
sentences.zh: 那是法国王权伟大的中心。

sentences.en: And the King of France is therefore a kind of brooding, slightly ambivalent presence.
sentences.zh: 因此，法国国王成了一种令人忧虑、态度有些矛盾的存在。

sentences.en: The Dukes have always been kind of essentially loyal to the King of France.
sentences.zh: 公爵们基本上一直对法国国王保持着效忠。

sentences.en: And the King of France has shown favor to them.
sentences.zh: 而法国国王也对他们表现出青睐。

sentences.en: But the risk is, is that if they seem too powerful, then the King may turn against them.
sentences.zh: 但风险在于，如果他们显得太过强大，国王可能会翻脸不认人。

sentences.en: So that's, that's an obvious risk.
sentences.zh: 所以，这是一个显而易见的风险。

sentences.en: And then on the Western flank of Normandy,
sentences.zh: 而在诺曼底的西线，

sentences.en: we've already mentioned the Dukes of Brittany and the Bretons are seen rather like the Romans used to see the ancient Britons as just complete barbarians.
sentences.zh: 我们已经提到了布列塔尼公爵，布列塔尼人在诺曼人眼中的形象，就像罗马人过去看待古代不列颠人那样，完全就是野蛮人。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So a Norman writer describes them as an uncivilized and quick tempered people lacking any manners and rather as the Romans did at talking about the Britons goes on about how they like to drink milk.
sentences.zh: 因此，一位诺曼作家将他们描述为一个不文明、脾气暴躁、毫无礼貌的民族，就像罗马人在谈论不列颠人时喋喋不休地谈论他们如何喜欢喝牛奶一样。

sentences.en: Well, you know, my views on that, my sister-in-law went out with a man called Paddy and he only drank milk.
sentences.zh: 好吧，你知道我对这件事的看法，我嫂子曾和一个叫帕迪的男人交往，而他只喝牛奶。

sentences.en: We went with them to Lisbon and he only drank milk and they don't, the Portuguese aren't really into drinking milk.
sentences.zh: 我们和他们一起去里斯本，他只喝牛奶，而葡萄牙人其实并不习惯喝牛奶。

sentences.en: So it was a total washout.
sentences.zh: 所以那真是一次彻底的泡汤。

sentences.en: And I've always been bitter about it since then.
sentences.zh: 从那以后我一直对此耿耿于怀。

sentences.en: I mean, I didn't drink milk.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我不喝牛奶。

sentences.en: The Normans do in the long run, they go and besiege and take Lisbon, don't they, in the Second Crusade.
sentences.zh: 诺曼人从长远来看，他们去围攻并占领了里斯本，不是吗，在第二次十字军东征中。

sentences.en: This is what happens if you just, if you, yeah, if you get involved with this milk drinking business, all kinds of horrors will follow.
sentences.zh: 这就是你如果不小心，如果你，是的，如果你卷入了这个喝牛奶的破事，各种恐怖的事情就会接踵而至。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So the Bretons are a constant challenge, but the most dangerous adversaries of the Norman Dukes are the Counts of Anjou who lie to the south and Anjou is centred on the Loire.
sentences.zh: 所以布列塔尼人是个持久的挑战，但诺曼公爵最危险的对手是南方的安茹伯爵，安茹以卢瓦尔河为中心。

sentences.en: And these are Counts, not Dukes.
sentences.zh: 他们是伯爵，而不是公爵。

sentences.en: So you might think, well, they're slightly second division.
sentences.zh: 所以你可能会想，他们大概算二流角色吧。

sentences.en: And there's an additional reason why it might seem slightly puzzling that the Counts of Anjou are such a menace because there is actually a buffer zone between Normandy and Anjou,
sentences.zh: 还有一个额外的原因让人觉得安茹伯爵成为如此巨大的威胁有些令人费解，因为诺曼底和安茹之间其实存在着一个缓冲地带，

sentences.en: which is the county of Maine.
sentences.zh: 那就是曼恩伯国。

sentences.en: So Le Mans, as in the motor racing.
sentences.zh: 也就是勒芒，就像赛车比赛里的那个勒芒。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, obviously not in the 11th century, but that's all lying in the future.
sentences.zh: 当然不是在11世纪，但那都是以后的事了。

sentences.en: I'm glad you clarified that.
sentences.zh: 我很高兴你澄清了这一点。

sentences.en: Yeah, I can just make sure that's clear.
sentences.zh: 是的，我只想确保这一点很清楚。

sentences.en: So this is a buffer zone, but it is clear that the Counts of Anjou are in a way the most Norman rival that the Normans have.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个缓冲地带，但很显然，安茹伯爵在某种程度上是诺曼人所拥有最具诺曼特色的对手。

sentences.en: You could look at the Counts of Anjou and say, yeah, they have something of the predatory quality of the Dukes of Normandy.
sentences.zh: 你可以这样看待安茹伯爵：是的，他们有着诺曼底公爵那种掠夺者的特质。

sentences.en: Because like the Dukes of Normandy, they are relative upstarts, they're very ambitious, they're exceedingly brutal, and they're very cunning, very politically proficient.
sentences.zh: 因为就像诺曼底公爵一样，他们也是相对的暴发户，野心勃勃，极其残忍，而且非常狡猾、政治手腕高明。

sentences.en: And the Count of Anjou, as Robert rides off on his pilgrimage, going off to Jerusalem, is a gnarled, terrifying, completely brutal warlord called Fulknera.
sentences.zh: 当罗伯特骑马离去、前去耶路撒冷朝圣时，安茹伯爵是一个饱经沧桑、极其可怕、完全冷酷无情的军阀，名叫富尔克·内拉。

sentences.en: And his nickname is The Black.
sentences.zh: 他的绰号是“黑色富尔克”。

sentences.en: Fulk the Black, that's a great name.
sentences.zh: 黑色富尔克，这名字太棒了。

sentences.en: Fulknera the Black.
sentences.zh: 黑色富尔克内拉。

sentences.en: And he has been in power for essentially half a century.
sentences.zh: 而且他掌权基本上长达半个世纪。

sentences.en: So he succeeded his father back in 987.
sentences.zh: 所以他在公元987年左右继承了父亲的职位。

sentences.en: And over the course of the 50 years that he's been Count of Anjou, I mean, he again and again displays his capacity for violence and vengeance,
sentences.zh: 在他担任安茹伯爵的这50年间，我的意思是，他一次又一次地展现出他对于暴力和复仇的渴望，

sentences.en: and perhaps the most notorious episode from his life.
sentences.zh: 这或许是他一生中最臭名昭著的一段插曲。

sentences.en: So in the year 1000 itself, the great citadel in Angers, which is essentially his capital, gets seized and held against him.
sentences.zh: 就在公元1000年，昂热的那座大城堡——基本上是他的首都——遭到占领并被用来对抗他。

sentences.en: And what is shocking about this absolute stab in the back is that the person who has led the rebellion against him is Fulknera's own wife.
sentences.zh: 而这次背后捅刀子最令人震惊的是，领导这场叛乱的人竟然是富尔克内拉自己的妻子。

sentences.en: And the reason that she's done this is that Fulknera has realised that she's been having an affair with someone else.
sentences.zh: 她这么做是因为富尔克内拉发现她与别人有染。

sentences.en: So, I mean, Cooke holding someone like Fulknera is very, very foolish.
sentences.zh: 所以，我是说，库克去扣押像富尔克内拉这样的人是非常非常愚蠢的。

sentences.en: So he is not happy about this.
sentences.zh: 因此他对这件事很不高兴。

sentences.en: He sweeps into Angers.
sentences.zh: 他席卷昂热。

sentences.en: He storms the citadel.
sentences.zh: 他攻打城堡。

sentences.en: Absolute carnage.
sentences.zh: 绝对是一场大屠杀。

sentences.en: Most of Angers is laid to waste.
sentences.zh: 昂热的大部分地区沦为废墟。

sentences.en: And his wife is captured and burnt at the stake.
sentences.zh: 他的妻子被俘并在火刑柱上烧死。

sentences.en: And that is a very public statement that, you know, do not cross him.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常公开的宣示，你知道的，千万别招惹他。

sentences.en: But also what Fulk represents, and people like him represent, is something bigger than just the sort of the dynastic soap opera of 10th century politics.
sentences.zh: 但富尔克以及像他这样的人所代表的，不仅是10世纪政治中那种王朝肥皂剧般的宏大叙事。

sentences.en: He's not a blowhard.
sentences.zh: 他可不是个吹牛大王。

sentences.en: He's not just a kind of wild barbarian.
sentences.zh: 他也不仅仅是个狂野的蛮族。

sentences.en: There is a, is it fair to call it a revolution?
sentences.zh: 这里正在发生一场——称之为革命公平吗？

sentences.en: There is a massive transition in European military life underway at this point, of which the Normans will be the great beneficiaries and the embodiment.
sentences.zh: 此时欧洲的军事生活正在发生巨大的转变，诺曼人将成为这场转变的伟大受益者和化身。

sentences.en: And that transition comes about, of course, because, and here's what I think a crucial difference between France and England.
sentences.zh: 这种转变当然会发生，因为——我认为这是法国和英国之间的一个关键区别。

sentences.en: France is so divided and fragmented.
sentences.zh: 法国是如此的分裂和支离破碎。

sentences.en: It's competitive.
sentences.zh: 它是充满竞争的。

sentences.en: It's militarily competitive.
sentences.zh: 它是军事上竞争激烈的。

sentences.en: And that breeds technological change.
sentences.zh: 而这孕育了技术的变革。

sentences.en: So the 11th century in France particularly is a period of such transformation that I think it is not an exaggeration to call it a revolution.
sentences.zh: 因此，尤其是11世纪的法国，是一个经历如此巨大变革的时期，我认为称之为一场革命并不过分。

sentences.en: Europe's first great revolution.
sentences.zh: 欧洲的第一场伟大革命。

sentences.en: And it affects almost every aspect.
sentences.zh: 它影响了几乎每一个方面。

sentences.en: So we will see it's religious, it's social, it's cultural, but it is also military.
sentences.zh: 所以我们会看到，它是宗教的、社会的、文化的，但它也是军事的。

sentences.en: So just focusing specifically on the military revolution that is happening in France at this time, it is absolutely, as you say,
sentences.zh: 如果我们把焦点专门放在当时法国正在发生的军事革命上，正如你所说，它绝对是

sentences.en: a consequence of the breakdown of royal authority in France.
sentences.zh: 法国王权崩溃的结果。

sentences.en: And back in the time of Charlemagne, it's a prerogative of the king to set up fortifications, to build battlements.
sentences.zh: 早在查理曼大帝的时代，建立防御工事、修建城垛是国王的特权。

sentences.en: That's essentially his job.
sentences.zh: 那基本上就是他的工作。

sentences.en: But by the time the Carolingian dynasty, the dynasty of Charlemagne, has gone extinct in France and has been replaced by the Capetian dynasty,
sentences.zh: 但当加洛林王朝——查理曼大帝的王朝——在法国绝嗣并被卡佩王朝取代时，

sentences.en: the Capetians are struggling to hold on to their own territory.
sentences.zh: 卡佩王朝正在艰难地保卫他们自己的领土。

sentences.en: And so their fortifications, rather than expressing their ability to control the whole of France, are an index of the fact that they're losing control.
sentences.zh: 因此，他们的防御工事不仅没有表达出他们控制整个法国的能力，反而成了他们正在失去控制的标志。

sentences.en: And because they've lost control, it means that in lands beyond their own heartlands, other figures, the dukes, the counts, whoever,
sentences.zh: 正因为他们失去了控制，这意味着在他们核心领土之外的其他人物，无论是公爵、伯爵还是其他人，

sentences.en: they are starting now to build fortifications because the king is not in a position to stop them.
sentences.zh: 现在都开始建造防御工事了，因为国王已经无力阻止他们。

sentences.en: And if you think of France as kind of rotting wood, these fortifications are like fungi, like mushrooms sprouting up out of the wood.
sentences.zh: 如果你把法国想象成朽木，这些防御工事就像是真菌，像从木头里长出来的蘑菇。

sentences.en: And these are strange, unsettling structures.
sentences.zh: 这些是奇怪且令人不安的结构。

sentences.en: No one's ever seen anything quite like them before.
sentences.zh: 以前从来没有人见过类似的东西。

sentences.en: And these are structures that in French will come to be called chateaux, and in English, castles.
sentences.zh: 这些在法语中被称为城堡（chateaux），在英语中被称为城堡（castles）的建筑。

sentences.en: And the greatest castle builder of his generation is Faulknera.
sentences.zh: 而他那一代最伟大的城堡建造者就是富尔克内拉。

sentences.en: Castles are the basis of his power and his expansionism.
sentences.zh: 城堡是他权力和扩张主义的基础。

sentences.en: And it reflects a very cold-eyed insight, which is that you can use castles not just for defence, but for attack.
sentences.zh: 这反映了一种极其冷静的见解，那就是你不仅可以把城堡用于防御，还可以用于进攻。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: These are tools of dominance and oppression.
sentences.zh: 这些是统治和压迫的工具。

sentences.en: They're tools, they're symbols of surveillance and control, but they're also, you know, they're impregnable.
sentences.zh: 它们是工具，是监视和控制的象征，但它们也是，你知道的，坚不可摧的。

sentences.en: You put them on a hill or on a rocky outcrop or whatever it might be, and there's no way that the people in the surrounding countryside can storm,
sentences.zh: 你把它们建在山丘上、岩石露头上或者任何类似的地方，周围乡村的人根本无法攻打，

sentences.en: or very difficult for them to storm it.
sentences.zh: 或者说他们很难攻打。

sentences.en: You control that territory now once you put down your castle.
sentences.zh: 一旦你建起了城堡，你现在就控制了那片领土。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So, I mean, essentially, you can plant it in enemy territory, and you put it on a crag or whatever, a cliff.
sentences.zh: 所以，我的意思是，基本上，你可以把它安插在敌方领土上，把它建在峭壁或悬崖上。

sentences.en: And if you can't find a crag or a cliff, then you can, you know, you can build a great mound of earth that comes to be called a mott.
sentences.zh: 如果你找不到峭壁或悬崖，那么你就可以，你知道的，建造一座巨大的土堆，后来被称为“土墩城堡”（mott）。

sentences.en: But essentially, you're seizing territory that previously had had no value at all.
sentences.zh: 但基本上，你是在抢占以前毫无价值的领土。

sentences.en: But now it enables you to be proactive, because you can build a very rough castle, you know, out of wood.
sentences.zh: 但现在它使你能够采取主动，因为你可以用木头建造一座非常粗糙的城堡，你知道的。

sentences.en: It can be incredibly rudimentary.
sentences.zh: 它可以极其简陋。

sentences.en: We're not talking great towers of stone or anything like that.
sentences.zh: 我们谈论的不是巨大的石头塔楼或类似的东西。

sentences.en: But because people are not used to the idea of fortifications suddenly sprouting up,
sentences.zh: 但由于人们不习惯防御工事突然冒出来的想法，

sentences.en: it has an outsized effect on the ability of those who control these structures to then impose themselves and intimidate people who are all around them.
sentences.zh: 它对那些控制这些建筑的人施加影响并威吓周围所有人的能力产生了巨大的影响。

sentences.en: And once you've done that, once you've used these kind of makeshift structures, these castles, to grab an area of territory, and if you keep it, then, of course, in time, you can,
sentences.zh: 一旦你做到了这一点，一旦你用这种权宜之计的结构——这些城堡——抢占了一片领土，如果你守住了它，那么当然，假以时日，你可以，

sentences.en: I don't know, rebuild them in stone or whatever.
sentences.zh: 我不知道，用石头重建它们或者别的什么。

sentences.en: And this is what Faulknera has been doing.
sentences.zh: 这就是富尔克内拉一直在做的事情。

sentences.en: And so the result is that, you know, he's been in power for decades and decades and decades.
sentences.zh: 因此结果就是，你知道的，他掌权了几十年又几十年。

sentences.en: By the 1030s, Anjou has come to be shielded all along its frontiers by kind of great donjons built on their crags, built on their mottes, and they're essentially impregnable.
sentences.zh: 到了1030年代，安茹的边境全都被建立在峭壁和土墩上的巨大主塔所保护，它们基本上是坚不可摧的。

sentences.en: And it means, therefore, that Anjou itself is impregnable.
sentences.zh: 因此这意味着安茹本身就是坚不可摧的。

sentences.en: But because, of course, France is such a competitive arena, Anjou's neighbours then have to follow suit, don't they?
sentences.zh: 但是，由于法国是一个竞争激烈的竞技场，安茹的邻居们不得不效仿，不是吗？

sentences.en: So that by this point, or certainly by the time Robert goes off on his jaunt to the Holy Land, Normandy too has lots of castles.
sentences.zh: 所以在此时，或者至少在罗伯特去圣地游历时，诺曼底也有了许多城堡。

sentences.en: So you have to, because it's basically a harms race.
sentences.zh: 所以你不得不这么做，因为这基本上是一场军备竞赛。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But I guess the question then is, is there a kind of human dimension to this?
sentences.zh: 但我想问题在于，这其中是否存在某种人性维度？

sentences.en: And this is a really interesting story.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常有趣的故事。

sentences.en: Of course, because it's a military revolution that is also a social revolution.
sentences.zh: 当然，因为这是一场军事革命，同时也是一场社会革命。

sentences.en: So it is creating an entire new class of people, because these castles, obviously, to be effective, they have to be held by warriors who are very well armed,
sentences.zh: 所以它创造了一个全新的阶层，因为这些城堡要想起作用，显然必须由全副武装的勇士把守，

sentences.en: probably who have armour, you know, chain mail.
sentences.zh: 他们可能拥有盔甲，你知道的，链甲。

sentences.en: And they have to be mobile, because if you're using the castle as a base, then you need to be able to sweep across the surrounding territory and intimidate anyone there,
sentences.zh: 而且他们必须具有机动性，如果你把城堡用作基地，那么你需要能够横扫周围的领土并恐吓那里的任何人，

sentences.en: which effectively means that you need horses.
sentences.zh: 这实际上意味着你需要马匹。

sentences.en: And how are you going to pay for this?
sentences.zh: 你将如何为此支付费用？

sentences.en: How are you going to pay for the horses, the armour, the swords, and whatever, the lances?
sentences.zh: 你将如何支付马匹、盔甲、长剑以及各种长矛的费用？

sentences.en: The answer, obviously, is you're going to do it mafia style by extorting cash out of those who don't have horses and armour, which effectively means the local peasantry.
sentences.zh: 答案显然是，你要像黑手党那样，通过向没有马匹和盔甲的人勒索现金来做到这一点，这实际上意味着当地的农民。

sentences.en: And up until the 11th century in France, peasantry essentially had been scattered.
sentences.zh: 直到11世纪的法国，农民基本上还处于散居状态。

sentences.en: But now they get kind of herded like sheep or cattle into pens.
sentences.zh: 但现在他们像绵羊或牛一样被赶进畜栏里。

sentences.en: And these pens are what come to be called villages.
sentences.zh: 这些畜栏就是后来被称为村庄的地方。

sentences.en: So the emergence of the castle also sees the emergence of the village.
sentences.zh: 因此，城堡的出现也伴随着村庄的出现。

sentences.en: And it's, I suppose, the kind of the classic image that people would have of the Middle Ages of, you know, a great castle and peasants and villages clustered around the castle.
sentences.zh: 我想，这就是人们对中世纪的经典印象，你知道的，一座大城堡，以及聚集在城堡周围的农民和村庄。

sentences.en: This is where that kind of image is originating.
sentences.zh: 这种印象就是从这里起源的。

sentences.en: And to contemporaries who are living through this, it's a completely shocking, unsettling, terrifying experience,
sentences.zh: 对于亲历这一切的当代人来说，这是一次完全令人震惊、不安和可怕的经历，

sentences.en: because suddenly you're getting these gangs of male clad thugs galloping through, you know,

sentences.en: They don't care about petty morals.
sentences.zh: 他们根本不在乎那些琐碎的道德。

sentences.en: Well, it is observed by the monk Rudolf Graeber, who is a brilliant source for this whole period.
sentences.zh: 好吧，修道士鲁道夫·格雷伯对此有过观察，他是这一时期极佳的史料来源。

sentences.en: It has always been their custom for as long as they've been settled in France to take as their princes, the offspring of concubines.
sentences.zh: 自他们在法国定居以来，立妾室所生的子嗣为王储，一直是他们的传统。

sentences.en: So, I guess you could kind of maybe say that at the Rolling Stones.
sentences.zh: 所以，我想你大概可以说这就像滚石乐队吧。

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think you probably could.
sentences.zh: 对，我想你大概可以这么说。

sentences.en: And people may remember that there was this kind of similar issue with Canute, wasn't there?
sentences.zh: 人们可能还记得，克努特身上也曾有过类似的问题，对吧？

sentences.en: And he had two wives or was one a concubine or anything.
sentences.zh: 他有两个妻子，还是其中一个是妾室之类的。

sentences.en: Although, it is interesting that times are definitely changing.
sentences.zh: 不过，有趣的是，时代确实在变。

sentences.en: So, views on marriage are also part of this great revolutionary process that is kind of picking up speed at this time.
sentences.zh: 因此，对婚姻的看法也是这一时期正在加速推进的伟大革新进程的一部分。

sentences.en: And the Normans are really actually kind of starting to buy into this.
sentences.zh: 而诺曼底人实际上也确实开始接受这一点了。

sentences.en: The fact that William's father had gone on pilgrimage is kind of evidence of that.
sentences.zh: 威廉的父亲曾去朝圣，就是这种转变的证明。

sentences.en: They are very, very pious Christians and increasingly anxious not to seem on the wrong sides of this kind of great moral revolution.
sentences.zh: 他们是非常虔诚的基督徒，并且越来越急切地想要避免站在这种伟大的道德革命的对立面。

sentences.en: And this combines with a sense that the best way for a noble family to pass on its patrimony is not to have a divided inheritance.
sentences.zh: 这与一种观念不谋而合：贵族家庭传承祖产的最佳方式是不实行遗产分割。

sentences.en: So, you remember when we talked about the Franks,
sentences.zh: 所以，还记得我们谈论法兰克人时吗？

sentences.en: you were expressing surprise that the Frankish kings and emperors kept dividing up their patrimony between their sons and thinking,
sentences.zh: 你当时对法兰克国王和皇帝们不断在儿子之间分割祖产感到惊讶，心想：

sentences.en: well, why haven't they sussed out that this is a bad thing to do?
sentences.zh: “好吧，他们怎么还没意识到这是一件坏事呢？”

sentences.en: This is, again, is the period where they are starting to work that out.
sentences.zh: 这同样也是他们开始明白这一点的时期。

sentences.en: So, the royal dynasty, the Capetian dynasty has worked this out.
sentences.zh: 所以，王室王朝，也就是卡佩王朝已经意识到了这一点。

sentences.en: And it seems that Robert, the Duke of Normandy, who's just died, he had worked it out as well.
sentences.zh: 看来刚刚去世的诺曼底公爵罗伯特也意识到了这一点。

sentences.en: So, after he has fathered William, he doesn't take a wife.
sentences.zh: 因此，在生下威廉之后，他没有再娶妻。

sentences.en: And it's probable the reason he does this is he doesn't want to have a divided inheritance.
sentences.zh: 他这样做的原因很可能是因为他不想分割遗产。

sentences.en: He doesn't want anyone to doubt that William is his heir.
sentences.zh: 他不想让任何人怀疑威廉是他的继承人。

sentences.en: Well, no one does doubt, although William is only eight years old.
sentences.zh: 好吧，确实没有人怀疑，尽管威廉当时只有八岁。

sentences.en: So, inevitably, the early years of his, in inverted commas, reign are going to be very bloody and contested.
sentences.zh: 因此，不可避免地，他在加号里的“统治”早年将充满血腥和争斗。

sentences.en: I mean, whatever he does and, you know, how many eight-year-olds are prepared to take the reigns of this warrior state?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，无论他做什么，你知道的，有多少八岁的孩子准备好接掌这个战士国家的大权呢？

sentences.en: But I think if there'd been, you know, two other brothers, maybe from a legitimate source, then that would have been a real source of instability.
sentences.zh: 但我想，如果当时还有另外两个可能出身合法的兄弟，那将成为真正的动荡之源。

sentences.en: But you're right.
sentences.zh: 不过你是对的。

sentences.en: I mean, he's in a terrible position.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他的处境糟透了。

sentences.en: And a contemporary chronicler notes as a sign how, forgetful of their loyalties,
sentences.zh: 一位当代的编年史家记录了一个迹象，说明他们是如何忘恩负义的，

sentences.en: many Normans set about piling up mounds of earth and then constructing fortified strongholds on them for themselves.
sentences.zh: 许多诺曼底人开始堆起土丘，然后在上面为自己建造坚固的防御工事。

sentences.en: So, these are the castles being used as tools of anarchy, basically.
sentences.zh: 所以，这些城堡基本上都被用作无政府状态的工具。

sentences.en: The motts, the mounds of earth and the baileys, the towers that are put on top of them.
sentences.zh: 也就是方锥台城堡——土丘，以及贝利城堡——建在土丘顶部的塔楼。

sentences.en: And, essentially, rival warlords within a dukedom building castles is a terrible sign.
sentences.zh: 从本质上讲，公国内的敌对军阀们大兴土木修建城堡，是一个极其糟糕的征兆。

sentences.en: It's a sign of state breakdown.
sentences.zh: 这是国家崩溃的信号。

sentences.en: And the fact that these warlords have their castles means that they can launch raiding parties on their rivals.
sentences.zh: 这些军阀拥有城堡，意味着他们可以向死敌发动突袭。

sentences.en: So, you get this craze throughout the early years of William's dukedom for abducting foes.
sentences.zh: 因此，在威廉统治公国的早期，绑架敌人的狂热风靡一时。

sentences.en: So, there's a notorious case where one is abducted from his own wedding feast, carried off, blinded, castrated.
sentences.zh: 有一个臭名昭著的案例：一个人在自己的婚礼宴会上被绑走，然后惨遭阉割和弄瞎双眼。

sentences.en: You know, that's not a good start to a wedding.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这对于婚礼来说可算不上什么好开头。

sentences.en: So, people are literally neutering the opposition.
sentences.zh: 所以，人们简直是在对政敌进行物理阉割。

sentences.en: And anarchy is spreading across Normandy.
sentences.zh: 无政府状态正在诺曼底蔓延。

sentences.en: And it's absolutely terrible time and will always be remembered as the worst time that Normandy ever endured.
sentences.zh: 这是一个绝对可怕的时代，并将永远被铭记为诺曼底经历过的最黑暗的时期。

sentences.en: And what about William?
sentences.zh: 那威廉呢？

sentences.en: I mean, he's only eight.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他才八岁。

sentences.en: What's he doing on all this?
sentences.zh: 他在这一切当中都在做些什么？

sentences.en: He's presumably not going around castrating people.
sentences.zh: 他大概不会到处去阉割别人吧。

sentences.en: No, and he's not without support.
sentences.zh: 没有，而且他并非孤立无援。

sentences.en: So, he does have, you know, he has the backing of the powerful men in his own family, the church hierarchy in Normandy.
sentences.zh: 所以，他确实拥有，你知道的，他得到了家族中权势人物以及诺曼底教会高层的支持。

sentences.en: They stay loyal to him.
sentences.zh: 他们对他忠心耿耿。

sentences.en: And he has the support of the King of France.
sentences.zh: 而且他还得到了法国国王的支持。

sentences.en: And that, again, is not insignificant.
sentences.zh: 这一点同样不可忽视。

sentences.en: But it's not enough to prevent his childhood from being constantly shadowed by violence.
sentences.zh: 但这还不足以让他的童年免受暴力阴影的纠缠。

sentences.en: So, two of his guardians are hacked down in quick succession.
sentences.zh: 因此，他的两位监护人相继遭到砍杀。

sentences.en: His own tutor is murdered.
sentences.zh: 他自己的家庭教师也被谋杀了。

sentences.en: And there's one particularly notorious occasion where he's in a room and his steward is also in the room asleep.
sentences.zh: 有一个特别臭名昭著的时刻：当时他在一个房间里，他的管家也在同一个房间里睡着了。

sentences.en: And people barge in and they cut the throat of the steward and the blood spills out.
sentences.zh: 然后有人闯进来割断了管家的喉咙，鲜血四溅。

sentences.en: The young duke is asleep and he wakes up and finds...
sentences.zh: 年轻的公爵正在睡觉，他醒来后发现……

sentences.en: Oh, my God.
sentences.zh: 哦，天哪。

sentences.en: You know, he thinks he's wet himself, perhaps, or something.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他可能以为自己尿床了什么的。

sentences.en: Oh, no!
sentences.zh: 噢，不！

sentences.en: It's like the horse's head and the godfather.
sentences.zh: 这就像《教父》里的马头桥段一样。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, so terrible.
sentences.zh: 对啊，我是说，太可怕了。

sentences.en: But, of course, the point of that story is that they killed the steward, but they've left William alone.
sentences.zh: 但当然，那个故事的重点在于他们杀了管家，却留下了威廉独自一人。

sentences.en: People are not after William himself.
sentences.zh: 人们并不是在针对威廉本人。

sentences.en: They're exploiting the fact that he is not in a position to rein in this anarchy.
sentences.zh: 他们只是在利用他无力控制这场混乱的局面这一事实。

sentences.en: But they're not targeting him for elimination.
sentences.zh: 但他们并没有把消灭他作为目标。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And I suppose you could say that the process of living through these horrors, I mean, it's stealing him, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 我想你可以说，经历这些恐怖事物的过程，我是说，它在磨炼他的意志，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, it's a good...
sentences.zh: 对，这倒是个好……

sentences.en: But, you know, we should think about this a little bit more carefully with our own royal family.
sentences.zh: 不过，你知道的，我们对自己的王室应该更仔细地考虑一下这个问题。

sentences.en: There may be a similar Spartan education.
sentences.zh: 也许会有一种类似的斯巴达式教育。

sentences.en: I thought with your enthusiasm for public schools that you might say that this could be a way to breed a hardy new elite.
sentences.zh: 我以为以你对公学教育的热情，你会说这可能会成为孕育强悍新精英的一种方式。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 一点没错。

sentences.en: Send them off and murder people.
sentences.zh: 把他们送出去大开杀戒。

sentences.en: This is what Prince Philip did with the king, Senator Gordonstone.
sentences.zh: 这就是菲利普亲王对国王做的事，戈登斯通参议员。

sentences.en: But there is actually, I said Spartan, but, I mean, you said it in your notes.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，我刚才说的是斯巴达式，不过，我是说，你在笔记里也写了。

sentences.en: There is something Spartan about a Norman's education.
sentences.zh: 诺曼人的教育确实有那么点斯巴达式的意味。

sentences.en: So somebody like William, he is being trained from, really from birth, for war, for cruelty, for violence.
sentences.zh: 所以像威廉这样的人，他从小，真的是从出生起，就在接受战争、残忍和暴力的训练。

sentences.en: I mean, that is, these are the duties of a Norman, of a Norman man.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这些正是一个诺曼人、一个诺曼男儿的职责。

sentences.en: Yes, and indeed women.
sentences.zh: 是的，女性也同样如此。

sentences.en: So aristocratic girls are being raised in this environment where, you know, it's all sweat and iron and horses and hawking.
sentences.zh: 所以贵族女孩们也是在这种环境中长大的，你知道的，全都是汗水、钢铁、战马和训鹰。

sentences.en: So like a British public school for girls, actually.
sentences.zh: 所以其实就像是一所英国女子公学。

sentences.en: Pretty, yeah, pretty much.
sentences.zh: 差不多，对，几乎就是这样。

sentences.en: Horses, cruelty.
sentences.zh: 战马，残忍。

sentences.en: So arms and horses and the exercises of hunting and hawking, such are the delights of a Norman.
sentences.zh: 所以武器、战马以及狩猎和训鹰的训练，这些就是诺曼人的乐趣所在。

sentences.en: And these are, of course, the patterns of the upper classes that will seize power in Britain.
sentences.zh: 而这些，当然也是将在英国夺权的统治阶级的行为模式。

sentences.en: And to a large extent, still own most of the land to this day.
sentences.zh: 并且在很大程度上，直到今天他们依然拥有大部分土地。

sentences.en: So, yes, this is where it all begins.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，这一切就是从这里开始的。

sentences.en: And William himself, again, like a Spartan, is raised as part of a wolf pack.
sentences.zh: 而威廉本人，同样像个斯巴达人一样，是在狼群般的环境中抚养长大的。

sentences.en: So he's surrounded by kinsmen, by highborn friends.
sentences.zh: 因此他身边环绕着亲族和出身高贵的伙伴。

sentences.en: And these are called nuri.
sentences.zh: 这些人在当地被称为nuri。

sentences.en: So people who are young boys, young men, who are nourished at the side of the Duke.
sentences.zh: 也就是那些在公爵身边长大、受其抚育的年幼男孩和年轻人们。

sentences.en: And so they grow up thinking of themselves as William's brothers in arMs.
sentences.zh: 所以他们长大后，会把自己视作威廉的患难兄弟。

sentences.en: And, you know, this is a pack of carnivores being trained to despoil.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，这是一群正在接受掠夺训练的食肉动物。

sentences.en: And what are they learning?
sentences.zh: 他们在学些什么呢？

sentences.en: They are learning the skills that are very, very demanding for this new way of war.
sentences.zh: 他们在学习适应这种新战争方式极其严苛的技能。

sentences.en: So you have to learn how to handle a lance properly, to sit in a saddle and use a lance.
sentences.zh: 所以你必须学会如何正确地挥舞长矛，如何在马鞍上坐稳并使用长矛。

sentences.en: I mean, this is a new skill, a new requirement, takes a lot of training.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是一项新技能，一项新要求，需要大量的训练。

sentences.en: And, you know, it takes years to perfect.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，这需要数年时间才能精通。

sentences.en: But William and his nuri, his comrades, you know, this is what they're learning.
sentences.zh: 但威廉和他的nuri、他的战友们，你知道的，这就是他们在学习的东西。

sentences.en: And, of course, they're also trained in all the cutting edge military technology, of which castle building is the most obvious.
sentences.zh: 当然，他们也接受了所有最前沿的军事技术训练，其中最明显的当属修筑城堡。

sentences.en: And it's all about attack, about spoliation, about conqueSt.
sentences.zh: 这一切都围绕着进攻、掠夺和征服。

sentences.en: So, I mean, that reminds me a little bit of Alexander the Great and his companions being raised with their famously long Macedonian spears.
sentences.zh: 所以，我的意思是，这让我有点想起亚历山大大帝和他的伙伴们，他们正是带着他们那著名的马其顿长矛长大的。

sentences.en: And, you know, the arts of conquest and all of that kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 还有，你知道的，那些征服的艺术以及诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: However, there is a different dimension to this, because as you point out in your notes,
sentences.zh: 然而，这其中还有另一个层面，因为正如你在笔记中所指出的那样，

sentences.en: William is also being raised to be extremely pious, not to say almost fanatical in his attachment to the faith
sentences.zh: 威廉受到的教育也极其虔诚，对信仰的执着甚至可以说是近乎狂热，

sentences.en: and his belief that he is the embodiment of a kind of new kind of Christian faith, I guess.
sentences.zh: 并且他坚信自己是某种新型基督教信仰的化身，我想是的。

sentences.en: That, again, I think there's a kind of slight parallel there with Cromwell.
sentences.zh: 这让我觉得，其中再次与克伦威尔有着某种微弱的相似之处。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: He's able to commit what seem to be atrocities, but do so in the absolute conviction that he is fulfilling God's will.
sentences.zh: 他能够犯下看似暴行的罪行，但同时又绝对坚信自己是在履行上帝的意志。

sentences.en: And there is a kind of new type of militancy to this faith, for reasons that we maybe come to later in this series.
sentences.zh: 这种信仰带有某种新型的战斗性，其原因我们可能会在本系列的后面探讨。

sentences.en: But William absolutely is raised in the kind of the fervor, in the spirit flame of this sense.
sentences.zh: 但威廉绝对是在这种狂热中、在这种意识形态的精神烈焰中抚养长大的。

sentences.en: And he sees absolutely no contradiction between his vocation as a warrior and his duty to give his subjects peace,
sentences.zh: 而且他认为，自己作为一名战士的职业与赋予子民和平的职责之间，绝对没有任何矛盾，

sentences.en: because it's only as a warlord that he can stamp his authority on the Normans.
sentences.zh: 因为只有作为一个军阀，他才能将自己的权威强加于诺曼人。

sentences.en: If all the Normans are predators, then he has to establish himself as the top predator, as the apex predator.
sentences.zh: 如果所有的诺曼人都是掠夺者，那么他就必须把自己确立为顶级掠夺者、终极掠夺者。

sentences.en: And even the Normans themselves can recognise that it would probably be best for the dukedom if William is able to essentially slap down anyone who would think to rival him.
sentences.zh: 甚至诺曼人自己也能认识到，如果威廉能够基本上镇压任何妄图与他争高下的人，这或许对公国才是最好的。

sentences.en: So there's an English chronicler writing after the Norman conquest in an abbey in Normandy, who writes about the Normans, rather as you would about dogs, I think.
sentences.zh: 因此，有一位诺曼征服后在诺曼底某座修道院写作的英国编年史家，他对诺曼人的描写，我想就像你在写狗一样。

sentences.en: For discipline the Normans with justice and firmness, and they will prove themselves men of great valour, who press invincibly to the fore in arduous undertakings,
sentences.zh: 用公正和坚定去管纪律诺曼人，他们就会证明自己是极为勇猛的人，在艰巨的任务中无畏地冲向前线，

sentences.en: and proving their strength, fight resolutely to overcome all enemies.
sentences.zh: 展现他们的力量，坚决战斗以战胜所有敌人。

sentences.en: But without such rule, they tear each other to pieces and destroy themselves, for they hanker after rebellion, cherish sedition, and are ready for any treachery.
sentences.zh: 但如果没有这样的统治，他们就会自相残杀、同归于尽，因为他们渴望叛乱、煽动风暴，随时准备做出任何背叛行径。

sentences.en: And I think William undoubtedly thinks this, and it steals him in his determination not to tolerate any rival.
sentences.zh: 我想威廉毫无疑问也是这么认为的，这坚定了他绝不容忍任何对手的决心。

sentences.en: And the older he gets, the readier he is to kind of impose this authority on his war-torn dukedom, for the benefit, obviously, of people who don't want to live in anarchy
sentences.zh: 他年纪越大，就越准备好将这种权威强加于他那饱受战争蹂躏的公国，这显然是为了造福那些不想生活在无政府状态中、

sentences.en: and be abducted on their wedding day and castrated.
sentences.zh: 不想在婚礼当天被绑架并阉割的人们。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Now, let's move to two people who are witnesses to all this, who see all this happening.
sentences.zh: 现在，让我们转向两个目睹这一切、见证这一切发生的人。

sentences.en: They are not Norman-born.
sentences.zh: 他们并非诺曼人出身。

sentences.en: They are exiles at Williams Court.
sentences.zh: 他们是威廉宫廷中的流亡者。

sentences.en: And these are people that we mentioned last week, who are the heirs to the Anglo-Saxon bloodline that had ruled England for so long.
sentences.zh: 这些人就是我们上周提到过的，长期统治英格兰的盎格鲁-撒克逊血统的继承人。

sentences.en: The heirs of Kurdic, the so-called mythical founder of this bloodline.
sentences.zh: 也就是那个所谓血统神话创始者库尔迪克的继承人。

sentences.en: And these are the half-brothers of Edmund Ironside.
sentences.zh: 他们是“铁胆”埃德蒙的同父异母兄弟。

sentences.en: They are called Alfred and Edward.
sentences.zh: 他们叫阿尔弗雷德和爱德华。

sentences.en: They are the sons of Ethelred the Unready.
sentences.zh: 他们是“无准备者”埃塞尔雷德的儿子。

sentences.en: And they have been in Normandy since 1016.
sentences.zh: 他们自1016年起就一直在诺曼底。

sentences.en: So they were there for 20 years before William even succeeded, hanging around at the court.
sentences.zh: 所以在威廉甚至还没继位之前，他们就已经在那里待了20年，在宫廷里厮混。

sentences.en: What's been going on with them?
sentences.zh: 他们一直在忙些什么呢？

sentences.en: They've been hanging out in Normandy because they don't want Canute to murder them, essentially, despite the fact that their mother, Emma, is now married to Canute.
sentences.zh: 他们一直在诺曼底闲晃，因为他们基本上不想被克努特谋杀，尽管他们的母亲埃玛现在已经嫁给了克努特。

sentences.en: But she's kind of washed her hands of them.
sentences.zh: 但她已经有点不管他们了。

sentences.en: She doesn't care about them.
sentences.zh: 她根本不在乎他们。

sentences.en: She essentially sees them as losers.
sentences.zh: 她基本上把他们视为失败者。

sentences.en: She doesn't need to worry about them.
sentences.zh: 她不需要为他们操心。

sentences.en: And I think this isn't really surprising because Emma, I mean, she is a baggage.
sentences.zh: 我想这其实并不令人意外，因为埃玛，我的意思是，她是个累赘。

sentences.en: She is very hard-nosed.
sentences.zh: 她非常冷酷精明。

sentences.en: She's very calculating.
sentences.zh: 她非常善于算计。

sentences.en: And essentially, she's interested in upholding her power.
sentences.zh: 归根结底，她感兴趣的是维护自己的权力。

sentences.en: And she can see that there's no prospect of Edward or Alfred succeeding to a throne that has now been seized by a Danish monarchy.
sentences.zh: 而且她能看出，爱德华或阿尔弗雷德根本没有指望继承现在已被丹麦王室夺走的王位。

sentences.en: And therefore, the son that she is backing is her son by Canute, a guy called Hartha Canute.
sentences.zh: 因此，她所支持的儿子是她与克努特所生的儿子，一个叫哈绍·克努特的家伙。

sentences.en: That is the person that she needs to succeed her husband.
sentences.zh: 那才是她需要继承她丈夫的人。

sentences.en: Now, there is a complication because, of course, she has a deadly rival who is this other wife,
sentences.zh: 现在，这里有个复杂情况，因为当然，她有一个死敌，那就是另一个妻子、

sentences.en: concubine, whatever you want to call her, Alf Gifu from the Midlands, Canute's first wife, who Canute has set up in Denmark and who likewise has given Canute a son, Harold,
sentences.zh: 妾室，随便你怎么称呼她，来自米德兰兹的阿尔夫吉夫，克努特的第一任妻子，克努特把她安置在丹麦，她同样为克努特生了个儿子哈罗德，

sentences.en: who we'll call Harold Hareford, even though that nickname doesn't emerge until the 12th century.
sentences.zh: 我们管他叫“快足”哈罗德，尽管这个绰号直到12世纪才出现。

sentences.en: Even so, Emma has kind of advantages over Alf Gifu.
sentences.zh: 即便如此，埃玛对阿尔夫吉夫还是有点优势的。

sentences.en: She is Canute's principal wife.
sentences.zh: 她是克努特的正妻。

sentences.en: She's the Queen of England.
sentences.zh: 她是英格兰王后。

sentences.en: She's been anointed as such.
sentences.zh: 她曾为此受过膏礼。

sentences.en: And because of this, most of the power breakers in England, so the earls and so on,
sentences.zh: 正因如此，英格兰的大多数权力操纵者，比如伯爵们等等，

sentences.en: they accept that Hartha Canute is the legitimate heir, that he is the guy who properly should succeed Canute.
sentences.zh: 他们都接受哈绍·克努特是合法继承人，认为他才是理应继承克努特的人。

sentences.en: Although, if I can jump in at this point, is there not a slight regional dimension to this,
sentences.zh: 不过，如果我此时插话的话，这难道没有一点地区差异吗，

sentences.en: in that Emma and Hartha Canute tend to have the support of the kind of the big landers or the big men in Wessex.
sentences.zh: 因为埃玛和哈绍·克努特往往能得到威塞克斯的大地主或大人物的支持。

sentences.en: But you mentioned Alf Gifu.
sentences.zh: 但你提到了阿尔夫吉夫。

sentences.en: She's from the Midlands.
sentences.zh: 她来自米德兰兹。

sentences.en: And the Mercians are more likely to back her and her son, Harold Hareford.
sentences.zh: 麦西亚人更有可能支持她和她的儿子“快足”哈罗德。

sentences.en: Yes, but I still think that had Hartha Canute been on the scene when Canute dies,
sentences.zh: 是的，但我依然认为，如果克努特去世时哈绍·克努特正在现场，

sentences.en: then probably most of the Witan, most of the earls in England would have accepted Hartha Canute as king.
sentences.zh: 那么威贤会议的大多数成员、英格兰的大多数伯爵可能会接受哈绍·克努特为国王。

sentences.en: The problem is, however, it doesn't turn out like that.
sentences.zh: 然而问题是，事情并没有这样发展。

sentences.en: We're a few months on from the death of Robert the Magnificent in Nicaea.
sentences.zh: 距离伟大的罗伯特在尼西亚去世已经过去几个月了。

sentences.en: It's the autumn of 1035, Canute dies, and the timing is an absolute disaster for Emma.
sentences.zh: 那是1035年的秋天，克努特去世了，这个时机对埃玛来说简直是一场绝对的灾难。

sentences.en: Because as you say, Hartha Canute is in Denmark, and Harold Hareford is in England.
sentences.zh: 因为正如你所说，哈绍·克努特在丹麦，而“快足”哈罗德在英格兰。

sentences.en: So he is the guy on the scene.
sentences.zh: 所以他才是身处现场的那个人。

sentences.en: And what makes it even worse, Emma sends kind of frantic messages to her son saying, you know, come here, come and get the throne.
sentences.zh: 更糟糕的是，埃玛给她的儿子发去了急信，你知道的，让他来这里，来夺取王位。

sentences.en: But he can't, because he's having to deal with a revolt in Norway.
sentences.zh: 但他来不了，因为他必须应对挪威的一场起义。

sentences.en: I mean, it's kind of interesting, because it's almost like he's running an election.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这挺有意思的，因为这几乎就像他在参加竞选一样。

sentences.en: He has to wine and dine all the various members of the Witan to try and persuade them that he should succeed as king of England and that Hartha Canute should be binned.
sentences.zh: 他必须设宴款待威贤会议的各个成员，试图说服他们自己应该继承英格兰国王之位，而哈绍·克努特应该被抛弃。

sentences.en: And Emma is likewise frantically campaigning for Hartha Canute to succeed.
sentences.zh: 埃玛同样也在拼命为哈绍·克努特的继位开展竞选活动。

sentences.en: So she spreads rumours that Harold was actually a changing, that he was the son of a servant woman, therefore not remotely legitimate, not the son of Canute at all.
sentences.zh: 于是她散布谣言，说哈罗德其实是个调包婴儿，是一个女仆的儿子，因此根本谈不上合法，根本就不是克努特的儿子。

sentences.en: And when this doesn't work, she barricades herself in Winchester, which is the place where the coronation would happen.
sentences.zh: 当这一招不管用时，她把自己 barricaded（封锁）在温彻斯特——也就是举行加冕典礼的地方。

sentences.en: To try and stop Harold from kind of sneaking in and having himself crowned there.
sentences.zh: 试图阻止哈罗德悄悄溜进来并在那里给自己加冕。

sentences.en: But then Elf Gifu turns up on the scene.
sentences.zh: 但随后阿尔夫吉夫出现在了现场。

sentences.en: She's sailed from Denmark.
sentences.zh: 她从丹麦乘船前来。

sentences.en: So bizarrely, she's in Denmark with her rival, with Hartha Canute.
sentences.zh: 所以说来也怪，她和她的对手哈绍·克努特一起在丹麦。

sentences.en: It's all mixed up.
sentences.zh: 这全乱套了。

sentences.en: But Elf Gifu is very proactive, hates Emma, wants her boy to succeed.
sentences.zh: 但阿尔夫吉夫非常积极主动，讨厌埃玛，一心想让自己的儿子继位。

sentences.en: So she does come sailing over.
sentences.zh: 所以她确实乘船赶了过来。

sentences.en: And she's very good at campaigning.
sentences.zh: 而且她非常擅长搞竞选。

sentences.en: She wines and dines all the various erls and jarls and people, all the members of the Witan, urging them to choose Harold as king.
sentences.zh: 她设宴款待了各个伯爵、雅尔以及所有人，也就是威贤会议的所有成员，敦促他们选择哈罗德为国王。

sentences.en: And because, as you said, there are people in England, particularly in Mercia, who instinctively do want to back Elf Gifu's relatives being among them.
sentences.zh: 而且正如你所说，英格兰有人，尤其是麦西亚人，本能地就想支持阿尔夫吉夫——她的亲戚也在其中。

sentences.en: She's very well connected in Mercia.
sentences.zh: 她在麦西亚有着极广的人脉。

sentences.en: And essentially, the momentum is all with Harold.
sentences.zh: 从根本上说，所有的势头都在哈罗德那边。

sentences.en: And so he marches on Winchester, where Emma has barricaded herself.
sentences.zh: 于是他向埃玛自守的温彻斯特进军。

sentences.en: Emma realises it's all up for her.
sentences.zh: 埃玛意识到自己全完了。

sentences.en: She runs away, leaves Winchester.
sentences.zh: 她逃跑了，离开了温彻斯特。

sentences.en: And Harold seizes what the Anglo-Saxon chronicle describes as all King Canute's best valuables.
sentences.zh: 而哈罗德夺取了盎格鲁-撒克逊编年史所描述的“英格兰国王所有的最佳财宝”。

sentences.en: Essentially, the coronation regalia.
sentences.zh: 基本上就是加冕王权法器。

sentences.en: So he's got what he needs now to be crowned.
sentences.zh: 所以他现在得到了加冕所需的全部东西。

sentences.en: If we stop the story there, Emma and Hartha Canute are on one side, and they look like they've loSt.
sentences.zh: 如果我们把故事停在这里，埃玛和哈绍·克努特站在一边，看起来他们已经输了。

sentences.en: And on the other side, Elf Gifu and her son, Harold Harefoot, looks like this bloke Harefoot, even though it's not his name.
sentences.zh: 而另一边，阿尔夫吉夫和她的儿子“快足”哈罗德——虽然这不是他的名字，但看起来就像这个叫“快足”的家伙。

sentences.en: He's going to be king, and he's got it all going on for him.
sentences.zh: 他要当国王了，而且一切都对他的胃口。

sentences.en: So now Emma's going to be out in the cold.
sentences.zh: 所以现在埃玛要被晾在一边了。

sentences.en: And she does something that I think is absolutely bonkers at this point.
sentences.zh: 而她在这个时候做出了一件我认为绝对疯狂的事。

sentences.en: And she drops her candidate, her son, and says, well, it wasn't really about him in the first place, actually.
sentences.zh: 她抛弃了她的候选人、她的儿子，并说，好吧，其实一开始也不是为了他。

sentences.en: It's more about me.
sentences.zh: 主要还是为了我。

sentences.en: So now she digs out the two losers from Normandy and says, what about these?
sentences.zh: 所以现在她把那两个来自诺曼底的失败者给挖了出来，说：这两个怎么样？

sentences.en: It throws them into the mix.
sentences.zh: 她把他们重新塞回了乱局之中。

sentences.en: I know.
sentences.zh: 我知道。

sentences.en: She's such an entertainingly horrible and ruthless character.
sentences.zh: 她真是一个有趣又可怕、冷酷无情的角色。

sentences.en: Because, of course, it's incredibly risky for these two lads to come over to England.
sentences.zh: 因为当然，这两个小伙子来英格兰风险极高。

sentences.en: A, they haven't been in England for 20 years.
sentences.zh: 第一，他们已经20年没来过英格兰了。

sentences.en: But they haven't seen her for 20 years either.
sentences.zh: 但他们也20年没见过她了。

sentences.en: I mean, they have no relationship with her whatsoever.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们和她之间根本没有任何关系。

sentences.en: But she's like, right, you two now.
sentences.zh: 但她却觉得：好啦，现在轮到你们俩了。

sentences.en: I actually am going to start sending you Christmas cards.
sentences.zh: 我实际上要开始给你们寄圣诞贺卡了。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's absolutely mad.
sentences.zh: 对，这简直太疯狂了。

sentences.en: But they do come in answer to their mother's requeSt.
sentences.zh: 但它们确实是应母亲的要求而来的。

sentences.en: I guess they kind of feel, well, maybe there's an opening here for us to come back.
sentences.zh: 我猜他们大概觉得，嗯，也许我们这里有机会卷土重来。

sentences.en: So the first to arrive is the eldest, Edward.
sentences.zh: 所以第一个到达的是长子爱德华。

sentences.en: And he lands at Southampton.
sentences.zh: 他在南安普顿登陆。

sentences.en: But, I mean, the welcoming committee is not all it might be.
sentences.zh: 但是，我的意思是，欢迎委员会可没那么大排场。

sentences.en: He has a look at it and he thinks, oh, God, I'm out of here.
sentences.zh: 他看了一眼，心想，哦，天哪，我得赶紧离开这儿。

sentences.en: And he sails back to Normandy.
sentences.zh: 于是他扬帆起航回到了诺曼底。

sentences.en: And then shortly after that, Alfred makes his own crossing and he lands, immediately gets captured.
sentences.zh: 在那之后不久，阿尔弗雷德也渡海而来，他刚一登陆就立刻被俘了。

sentences.en: And him and all his followers are treated very, very brutally.
sentences.zh: 他和他的所有追随者都受到了非常非常残酷的虐待。

sentences.en: So we're told that his followers are stalled into slavery, cruelly murdered, laid down with chains, blinded, mutilated and scalped.
sentences.zh: 据说他的追随者有的被卖为奴隶，有的被残忍杀害，戴上沉重的枷锁，弄瞎双眼、肢解并剥皮。

sentences.en: And Alfred himself is taken to Ely in the middle of East Anglia, kind of on an island surrounded by the Fens.
sentences.zh: 阿尔弗雷德本人则被带到了东盎格利亚中部的伊利，那是个四周环绕着沼泽的小岛。

sentences.en: And there he is blinded and he dies soon afterwards of his wounds.
sentences.zh: 在那里他被挖去双眼，不久后便因伤重身亡。

sentences.en: And mummy...
sentences.zh: 还有妈妈……

sentences.en: Doesn't care.
sentences.zh: 她根本不在乎。

sentences.en: Well, mummy does care because now, you know, that attempt's failed.
sentences.zh: 好吧，妈妈其实是在乎的，因为现在你知道的，那个计划失败了。

sentences.en: So she runs away to Flanders.
sentences.zh: 于是她逃到了法兰德斯。

sentences.en: And, of course, everyone is saying she's behaved terribly.
sentences.zh: 当然，每个人都在说她表现得太糟糕了。

sentences.en: I mean, this is monstrous behaviour.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这简直是禽兽不如的行为。

sentences.en: And so she starts kind of, again, spinning frantically and saying, actually, it wasn't me who sent, you know, the letters to Edward and Alfred.
sentences.zh: 于是她又开始疯狂狡辩，说其实写信给爱德华和阿尔弗雷德的不是她。

sentences.en: It was Harold Harefoot who did it.
sentences.zh: 是飞脚哈罗德干的。

sentences.en: There's no truth in that.
sentences.zh: 这根本不是真的。

sentences.en: That's just a lie.
sentences.zh: 这纯属谎言。

sentences.en: No, because it was her seal on it.
sentences.zh: 不对，因为上面盖着她的印玺。

sentences.en: And she's saying, oh, he faked my seal.
sentences.zh: 而她却说，哦，那是他伪造了我的印玺。

sentences.en: You know, he hacked my account.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他黑了我的账号。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That's terrible.
sentences.zh: 这太恶劣了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: And in 1038, when Emma summons Edward to go and join her in Flanders, he says, no way.
sentences.zh: 1038年，当埃玛召唤爱德华去法兰德斯与她会合时，他断然拒绝了。

sentences.en: I've had enough.
sentences.zh: 我受够了。

sentences.en: Well, you wouldn't.
sentences.zh: 好吧，换作谁都不会去。

sentences.en: I mean, that's not a mother you want to be reunited with, frankly.
sentences.zh: 坦白讲，这可不是那种你会想与之团聚的母亲。

sentences.en: But here's the thing, right?
sentences.zh: 但关键是，对吧？

sentences.en: So this has been a mad story so far.
sentences.zh: 所以到目前为止，这是一个极其疯狂的故事。

sentences.en: All these people called Harefoot and Harthakneet and whatnot and just ridiculous twists.
sentences.zh: 所有这些叫飞脚和哈绍克努特之类名字的人，还有各种荒谬的转折。

sentences.en: But now there is another insane twist to this story, which, you know, if you were the Game of Thrones script writer, you'd say, come on, this is a bit much.
sentences.zh: 但现在这个故事又迎来了一个疯狂的转折，如果你是《权力的游戏》的编剧，你大概会说，拜托，这未免有点太夸张了。

sentences.en: So Harold Harefoot basically has won.
sentences.zh: 所以飞脚哈罗德基本上赢了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: He's king.
sentences.zh: 他成了国王。

sentences.en: The years go by.
sentences.zh: 岁月流逝。

sentences.en: He is 25 years old.
sentences.zh: 他年仅25岁。

sentences.en: He could live for another 40 years.
sentences.zh: 他可能还能再活40年。

sentences.en: You know, a lot of English listeners to this podcast may be thinking, I've actually never heard of this bloke, Harold Harefoot.
sentences.zh: 听这个播客的很多英国听众可能会想，我其实从来没听说过这家伙——飞脚哈罗德。

sentences.en: I think there's a case for saying he's kind of the most obscure king who's ever ruled England.
sentences.zh: 我认为完全可以说他是有史以来统治过英格兰的最默默无闻的国王。

sentences.en: People know nothing about him.
sentences.zh: 人们对一无所知。

sentences.en: I've never heard of him.
sentences.zh: 我从未听说过他。

sentences.en: I know nothing about him.
sentences.zh: 我对一无所知。

sentences.en: I don't believe this man was ever king of England.
sentences.zh: 我不相信这个人曾经做过英格兰国王。

sentences.en: And the reason for that is the sources are so kind of fragmentary and vague, but also unbelievable twiSt.
sentences.zh: 原因在于历史资料非常碎片化且模糊，而且还有一个难以置信的转折。

sentences.en: He drops dead out of nowhere for no good reason.
sentences.zh: 他莫名其妙地突然暴毙了。

sentences.en: Yet another character in this story who drops dead out of from nowhere.
sentences.zh: 故事中又一个莫名其妙暴毙的角色。

sentences.en: Yeah, so he's gone and this is obviously brilliant news for Harthacnut and for Emma.
sentences.zh: 是的，所以他死了，这对哈绍克努特和埃玛来说显然是个天大的好消息。

sentences.en: So three months after the death of Harold Harefoot, Harthacnut lands in Kent and who should be with him?
sentences.zh: 因此，在飞脚哈罗德死后三个月，哈绍克努特在肯特登陆，而谁跟他在一起呢？

sentences.en: But his very, very self-satisfied mother, who's absolutely delighted.
sentences.zh: 正是他那位自我感觉极其良好、欣喜若狂的母亲。

sentences.en: So Harthacnut, to get to England, has had to agree quite stiff terms with the king of Norway.
sentences.zh: 为了到达英格兰，哈绍克努特不得不与挪威国王达成相当苛刻的条件。

sentences.en: So he abandons his claim to Norway for good.

sentences.zh: 因此，正当英格兰发生这一切的时候，威廉也迎来了成年。
